items.entity: Absolute beam dimensions Lx, Ly (element size)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the ratio Lx:Ly = 6:1, and Fig. 2a labels the sides with symbols. No absolute length or element size is stated. In 2-D with unit thickness and a nodal point load, compliance does not depend on absolute size. The layout also stays the same as long as rmin is taken in element units.
The paper never gives a thickness for the 2-D domain.

items.entity: Element counts 180 x 30 vs. the analysed right symmetric half
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says the domain is parameterized with Nex = 180 and Ney = 30, then says the right symmetric half is optimized. It does not say whether 180x30 covers the full 6:1 beam or the analysed half. App. B reproduces the same gSF m = 1 result (f0 = 0.0149, Mnd = 1.57%) with '90 x 30 ... symmetric half design domain'. However, the Table 12 caption says 'MBB beam is solved with 90 x 30' without mentioning the half, and App. B.1 meshes 'the MBB design domain' with 180 x 60.
readings: Full beam 180x30; analysed right half 90x30 with square elements (consistent with Lx:Ly = 6:1 and App. B)
Analysed half itself 180x30 with square elements (the full beam would then be 360x30, i.e. 12:1)

items.entity: Supports of the simply supported MBB beam (roller in the analysed right half)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only calls the problem 'a simply supported beam' (cf. Fig. 2a). The Table 2 discussion mentions a 'roller support' region, and the full designs (Fig. 4) mention 'roller and hinge'. The exact support position and extent (one corner node or a small patch) are shown only in Fig. 2a. The most consistent half-model setup is a symmetry condition (ux = 0) on the cut plus a roller (uy = 0) at the far bottom corner.
readings: Roller (uy = 0) at the single bottom-right corner node of the half model
Roller (uy = 0) spread over a few nodes (e.g. 2-4) at the right end of the bottom edge

items.entity: Downward point load at top mid-span, as applied to the half model
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'An external force (F) of magnitude 10^-3 unit is applied' at the midpoint of the top edge of the full beam. Sec. 4.1.1 analyses only the right half, and the text does not say whether the symmetry-line node of the half model gets the full 10^-3 or half of it. The reported f0 magnitude suggests the full 10^-3 was applied to the half model.
readings: F = 1e-3 downward at the top-left (symmetry-line) node of the half model (full-beam load 2e-3)

items.entity: Single-material volume fraction for Table 2, m = 1
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says 'For 1 material result, we use 1D SF with vf = 0.3', and Table 12 (m = 1) also lists 0.30. Table 2 itself prints no vf. The Fig. 7a legend (MBB, 1D SFs) and the Fig. 8 caption (MBB beam, Fig. 2a) list single-material MBB runs with both vf = 0.30 and vf = 0.40. The Table 2 Mnd of 1.57% matches Fig. 8a, which is the vf = 0.30 run.
Only a normalized Young's modulus is given (E = 1 for the single 1D-SF material, Sec. 4). Poisson's ratio is not stated anywhere in the paper.
Sec. 4 states that bilinear quadrilateral FEs are used, but never says whether the analysis is plane stress or plane strain.

items.entity: Minimum (void) stiffness Emin and the void-phase Em in Eq. 33
items.description: Sec. 3.1 / Eq. 33 describe Emin only as 'a very small stiffness' and give no value. Eq. 33 sums over all 2^n phases including the void, but the void's Em is not given. It has to be Emin (or the void term dropped); otherwise E becomes 0 in fully void elements.

items.entity: Which Table 2 run is the m = 1 example
items.description: The m = 1 row of Table 2 (Sec. 4.1.1, 'Qualifying the use of density and introduced projection filters') contains three different runs: CASE I (no density filter, f0 = 0.0172, Mnd = 6.36%), CASE II (density filter only, f0 = 0.0263, Mnd = 39.38%) and CASE III (density filter + projection, f0 = 0.0149, Mnd = 1.57%). The text treats the last column as the actual result, but 'Table 2, m = 1' alone does not pick one run.
readings: CASE III: density filter rmin = 3.6 + modified tanh projection (eta = 0.5, beta 1 -> 32)
CASE II: density filter only, no projection

items.description: CASE I is defined only as 'No density filtering'. The text does not say whether the projection of Eq. 30 (eta = 0.5, beta continuation) is still applied to the unfiltered variables, or whether the raw variables go straight into Eq. 33.
readings: No density filter and no projection (raw variables, SIMP p = 3)
Projection (eta = 0.5, beta doubled every 75 iterations up to 32) applied to the unfiltered variables

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 sets rmin = 3.6 with no unit. Eq. 27-28 use a center-to-center distance Dis(j,k) without saying whether it is measured in element widths or in physical length, and the physical domain size is unknown.
readings: 3.6 in physical length units of whatever domain size is adopted (same as the first reading only if h = 1)

items.entity: Density-filter neighbourhood at domain edges / symmetry cut
items.description: Sec. 2.3 (Eq. 27-28) does not say how the filter is handled at boundaries. This matters most at the symmetry line of the half model, where the load is applied.
readings: Mirrored (symmetric) extension across the symmetry line, equivalent to filtering the full beam

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 gives no initial guess. Sec. 4.4.2 shows that different initial guesses give different topologies, and Sec. 4.4.3 uses xi = 0 for a different case.
readings: Uniform solid density equal to vf = 0.3 (xi = -0.4 or +0.4 depending on the vertex convention)

items.description: MMA [43] is named (Sec. 3.3), with at most 400 iterations and the objective scaled by nf = min(10/obj, 100) from loop 1 (about 100 here). The move limit, asymptote initialization/adaptation and the a0, a_i, c_i, d_i constants are not given. Note that the variables range over [-1, 1].
readings: Svanberg default mmasub settings (asyinit 0.5, asyincr 1.2, asydecr 0.7, move 0.5, a0 = 1, a = 0, c = 1000, d = 1)
Same, but with a move limit of 0.2 on xi
Same, but with a move limit of 0.1 on xi

items.description: Sec. 4 says only 'The maximum number of MMA iterations is set to 400' and gives no convergence tolerance. Because beta doubles every 75 iterations, it reaches 32 only at about iteration 375, so stopping earlier would leave a less crisp design.
readings: Stop earlier once beta = 32 and max|delta xi| (or the relative objective change) is below about 0.01

items.entity: 1D material element: which end of xi is the solid phase
items.description: Eq. 4 sets x11 = -1, x12 = +1, but the base case of the induction proof (Sec. 2.1.2, Eq. 11) uses x11 = +1, x12 = -1. Neither place says which of the two phases is void and which is the E = 1 material. Because eta = 0.5 makes the projection symmetric, the choice matters only when combined with a non-zero initial xi.

items.entity: Definition of the reported objective f0 in Table 2
items.description: Sec. 3.3 defines f0 = 1/2 U^T K U, and Sec. 4 says the objective is multiplied by nf = min(10/obj, 100) in every iteration. The paper does not say whether Table 2's f0 (e.g. 0.0149) is the raw strain energy, the compliance F^T U, or the nf-scaled value. A value of about 1e-2 with F = 1e-3 and E = 1 points to the nf-scaled strain energy. In Table 12, the O-SIMP m = 1 value (0.0296) is about twice the gSF / Ex-SIMP value.
readings: f0 = 100 x (1/2) F^T U (nf-scaled strain energy)

locator: Sec. 4.1.1, the 2-D MBB beam, single-material case (Table 2, m = 1)
